learningObjective: Reason about when compile time should be reported alongside inference latency in benchmarks and how the choice affects fair comparison.

canonicalClaims.claim: Fair ML compiler benchmarks disclose compile time alongside inference latency because compile cost matters for iterative development, canary deploys, autoscaling and per-tenant compile scenarios; hiding it misleads readers even when steady-state latency is favorable.
conditions: The benchmark compares systems with different compile-time budgets.
The intended workflow is not exclusively steady-state serving of a single model.
nonImplications: Does not imply compile time must equal inference importance in every scenario.
Does not imply shorter compile is universally better.

misconceptions.claim: Compile time is always amortized to zero.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Canary, autoscaling, and per-tenant workloads amortize poorly.

misconceptions.claim: Compile time can be omitted because it's offline.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Offline cost affects release cadence and rollback speed; still meaningful to disclose.

misconceptions.claim: Two systems with equal inference latency are equivalent regardless of compile time.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Compile-cost differences shift developer velocity and deployment agility.

misconceptions.claim: Compile-time benchmarks require running compile on every request.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Compile time is measured separately; it does not need to be added to per-request latency.
